approach: Add one reading-gate check, `check_speed_timeline(reading, request)`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs. Wire it as one `step!(check_speed_timeline(reading, request));` line in `refusing_check`, right after `check_outcome_state`. A speed request is found from the request text with `request_words` (reading.rs:3503). Strong cues stand alone: faster, quicker, speedup, latency, `speed|speeds|sped|speeding` + `up`, `head start`, and a cut verb (cut, save, shave, trim, reduce, shorten, eliminate and their forms) within five words before a duration figure. Weak cues (slow/slower/slowest/slowly/slowdown, delay/delays/delayed, timing/timings) count only with a cut verb within five words before them or `too` right before them. So 'add a retry delay setting' and 'fix a timing attack' are not speed requests. For a speed request the reading needs an assumption whose trimmed text starts `Timeline:` (any case, as `code_surveys` does). Its clauses, split at `;` or a newline, must hold: (1) a clause naming a crates/ path (`names_crates_path`, reading.rs:3838); (2) a clause starting `stages:` with at least two entries in order, split at `,`, `->`, `→` or ` then `, where each entry's stage name is its first word that starts with a letter and is not a unit word, and each entry has a duration figure, unless the Timeline says 'no recorded timing' (the escape replaces only the durations, so stages are still required); (3) a clause with a place word (sits, slowest, longest, bottleneck) followed in that clause by one of the stage names, so the claimed delay is placed in a stage. The word 'delay' alone is not a place word. Refusals are one line starting 'the reading was refused because' and say what to write. The check reads only the reading and the request, so it is deterministic. Four more edits: a seventh `READING_RULES` line in briefs.rs; corpus cases and a declared-intended test; one fixed `Timeline:` assumption in the fake reader (fake.rs); and D163 plus a CHANGELOG entry. The fake line is a file beyond the listed deliverables, and it is unavoidable. The drain test at drain.rs:7008 sends 'Speed up planning...' through the real gate with the fake reader, so the fake reading must pass the gate. The fake's Timeline puts its crates/ path in a `;`-separated clause with an absence phrase, so `check_reading_references` skips it in the CLI fixture repo, which has no crates/ directory. The root cause named everywhere: the reading stage checked a request's own figures only if the reader chose to, so readings were planned around stated timings with no stage timeline from the code. The fix sits at the reading gate, where every speed request passes.

decisions.choice: Enforce at the reading gate: one `step!` in `refusing_check` (reading.rs:3226-3252), placed after `check_outcome_state`.
decisions.reason: Every reading passes `refusing_check`. The corpus mechanism (`every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case`, refusal_corpus.rs:1061) forces a refusing case per step. No model call is needed. A refused reading gets one re-read with the refusal text, so the reader learns what to write. The existing test `check_outcome_state_doc_names_root_cause_and_scope` (reading.rs:7725) needs `check_outcome_state` right after `check_governance_coverage`; a step after it leaves that position alone.

rejected.why: Prose only; the reader can ignore it, which is the failure. The 'mechanism' default requires a check. The reader token budget is 1997 of 2000 and the prompt file is out of scope.
By the planner the reading is already accepted and the criteria are fixed around the request's figure. Planner prompts are out of scope.
It runs after the producer built the wrong thing; the failure is in planning.

decisions.choice: The Timeline must hold a crates/ path, an ordered `stages:` list of at least two stages, a duration per stage, and a place word followed by a stage name. 'No recorded timing exists' replaces only the durations, never the stages or the place.
decisions.reason: This answers critic finding 3. The three introspections ask for 'each stage in order, its measured duration, and where the claimed delay sits'. The stage order and the place of the delay can be read from the code without run data; only the durations may be missing. The gate reads text only, so it checks the shape, not whether the figures are true; this is stated in the doc comment and D163.

rejected.option: A stock 'no recorded timing' phrase plus a crates/ path clears the check
rejected.why: One fixed sentence would clear every speed request without the reader writing the stage order, which is the cause.

rejected.option: Have Athena run the stages at reading time
rejected.why: Needs a build and test run per reading; unbounded cost; beyond one producer run.

rejected.option: Check only when the request holds a duration figure
rejected.why: The class includes 'make it faster' with no figure.

decisions.choice: Place words are sits, slowest, longest and bottleneck, and each must be followed in its clause by a stage name taken from the `stages:` list. 'delay' is not a place word.
decisions.reason: This answers critic finding 5. A reader echoing the request writes 'the delay' without placing it. Tying the place to a named stage forces the placement.

rejected.why: A Timeline such as 'the claimed delay is real' would pass without placing the delay in a stage.

decisions.choice: Weak cues (slow*, delay*, timing*) count only with a cut verb within five words before them or `too` right before. Strong cues (faster, quicker, speedup, latency, speed up, head start, cut verb plus a duration figure) stand alone.
decisions.reason: This answers critic finding 4. It keeps 'add a retry delay setting', 'fix a timing attack' and 'the slow path' out, and keeps 'still too slow' and 'reduce the delay' in. Corpus cases pin both sides. Cues are whole words over `request_words`, which already splits bullets, `1.`, `2)` and `(a)` parts and hyphens ('speed-up'), so 'slowloris', 'speedometer', 'quickstart' and 'timeline' do not match.

rejected.why: Common in requests that are not about speed; they would be refused until the reader writes a Timeline.

rejected.option: Substring match like the fake reader's SPEED_WORDS
rejected.why: Matches inside other words and drifts from the gate.

decisions.choice: Keep the crates/ path requirement and state the limit in D163: a target repository with no crates/ directory cannot meet the rule.
decisions.reason: This answers critic finding 6. It mirrors `check_code_survey`, and the reading's contract says the Timeline names the crates/ code read. Accepting any slash path would change the contract. The fake reader's own Timeline gets past the CLI fixture repo (no crates/) by using an absence phrase, not by loosening the rule. A non-crates generalisation is a named follow-up.

rejected.option: Accept any slash path the reading references
rejected.why: Widens the rule beyond the reading and the contract; `check_reading_references` checks existence only for known top directories.

decisions.choice: The fake reader (crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs:283) always adds one fixed assumption: 'Timeline: read crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs, which does not exist in a nested-run repository; stages: read, write; no recorded timing exists; the delay sits in write.' The fake carries a fixed string and no check logic. Always-on avoids a second cue list in athena-agent, which cannot call the gate.

demonstrations.method: Run the refusal corpus. New cases give a speed request and a reading with no Timeline assumption, and expect `Expected::Refuse("check_speed_timeline")`. Cases: 'speed-request-without-a-timeline' ('Move the call earlier to save 12 minutes.'), 'speed-word-in-a-dash-bullet', 'speed-word-in-a-star-bullet', 'speed-word-in-a-numbered-dot-part', 'speed-word-in-a-numbered-paren-part', 'speed-word-in-a-lettered-paren-part', 'retry-complaint-still-too-slow-without-a-timeline', 'root-cause-request-names-a-delay-without-a-timeline', plus the Timeline-defect refusals: no path, crate-relative path, one stage, a stage without a duration, no-recorded-timing with no stages, no place word, a place word with no stage after it, label not at the start, no label.
demonstrations.observes: `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` passes, so each of those cases is refused by `check_speed_timeline` and by no earlier check. `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` passes with the new step name in the extracted list. `speed_timeline_refusal_is_declared_intended` passes.
demonstrations.fails_without: Remove the `step!(check_speed_timeline(reading, request));` line and every Refuse("check_speed_timeline") case is accepted, so `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` reports 'expected Refuse("check_speed_timeline"), got accepted'. Keep the step but drop cue detection and the same cases fail. Drop the Timeline requirement and the defect cases fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `athena_core::reading::refusing_check` (reading.rs:3226, exists), called by `run(c)` in refusal_corpus.rs:942 (exists). Fixture: `case()` and `base_reading()` (refusal_corpus.rs:117,186, exist) with `repo_files()` injected as `Some(repo_files())` (exists). The new cases come from a new `speed_timeline_cases()` that step 6 adds to `cases()`. Guards: capability is Some and question is None. The base reading is class docs with content criteria, so no earlier check refuses. Input forms and their case ids: dash bullet `speed-word-in-a-dash-bullet`; star bullet `speed-word-in-a-star-bullet`; `1.` part `speed-word-in-a-numbered-dot-part`; `2)` part `speed-word-in-a-numbered-paren-part`; `(a)` part `speed-word-in-a-lettered-paren-part`; retry complaint `retry-complaint-still-too-slow-without-a-timeline` (and its `...-with-a-timeline` accept twin); a request that cites a job without relying on it `root-cause-request-names-a-delay-without-a-timeline` (with the cites-job-without-relying tag; and an accept twin); crate-relative path `timeline-with-a-crate-relative-path`; lookalike words `speed-word-lookalikes-are-not-speed-requests`. A brand word or environment variable read as a symbol is not read by this rule (it reads cue words and Timeline text only), so no case is added. Existing cases such as `steward-three-dash-bullets` are unchanged. The new cases are added by step 6.

demonstrations.method: The same corpus run holds accept cases: 'speed-request-with-a-timeline' (assumption 'Timeline: read crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs; stages: compile 9 min, check 40 s; the delay sits in compile.'); 'speed-request-timeline-says-no-recorded-timing' (stages named, no durations, 'no recorded timing exists', place given); the retry and root-cause requests with a Timeline; 'speed-request-question-reading-needs-no-timeline'; 'speed-word-lookalikes-are-not-speed-requests' ('Add a timeline view and a speedometer widget. Write a quickstart guide. Wait 30 seconds before the retry. Cover the slowloris case.'); and the critic's real-use pins 'add-a-retry-delay-setting-is-not-a-speed-request' ('Add a retry delay setting.') and 'fix-a-timing-attack-is-not-a-speed-request' ('Fix a timing attack in the login.'). Existing non-speed cases stay accepted. Unit tests in reading.rs run the detector and the check directly.
demonstrations.observes: All accept cases return None from `refusing_check`. The reading.rs unit tests `speed_requests_are_found_by_whole_word_cues_and_figures` and `a_timeline_assumption_needs_stages_durations_and_a_placed_delay` pass. They cover: accept; the no-timing escape with stages; skip when capability is None or a question is set; one-line errors starting 'the reading was refused because'; positive requests ('Make the check faster', 'Speed up planning', 'a speed-up of the run', 'Cut 5 minutes from the checks', 'reduce the delay', 'still too slow'); and negative requests ('Add a timeline view', 'a speedometer widget', 'a quickstart guide', 'the slowloris test', 'wait 30 seconds before the retry', 'Seen 3 time(s) in 3 jobs', 'add a retry delay setting', 'fix a timing attack').
demonstrations.fails_without: If the check refused every speed-word request regardless of the Timeline, `speed-request-with-a-timeline` would be refused. If bare delay/timing counted as cues, the two real-use pins would be refused. If the check applied to non-speed requests, `steward-three-dash-bullets` would be refused. Each makes `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `refusing_check`, and in unit tests `check_speed_timeline` directly (step 2 adds it). Fixtures: `case()`/`base_reading()` (exist) and `governed_reading` (reading.rs:7364, exists). The Timeline text is set on `reading.assumptions`. Precondition: the Timeline names only crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, which is in `repo_files()`, so `check_reading_references` does not refuse it.

demonstrations.method: A new corpus test reads reading.rs (`READING_SOURCE`, include_str, exists at refusal_corpus.rs:1016) and asserts that the exact line `step!(check_speed_timeline(reading, request));` is in the body of `refusing_check` directly after the `check_outcome_state` step. It also asserts that the doc paragraph above `pub fn check_speed_timeline(` is one `///` paragraph holding the root-cause sentence, the three job ids, 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.' and 'expected 5% of newly refused readings'. It mirrors `design_existing_code_refusal_is_declared_intended` (:1102).
demonstrations.observes: The test passes. The step line is present once. The doc comment holds 20261025-110525-8hzb, 20261025-034733-c453 and 20261025-190606-eebk, the root-cause wording, and the intended-rate sentences. `athena_core::reading::replay_declaration` returns share Some(5) for the text 'expected 5% of newly refused readings'.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the step line or the doc comment the string assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: `include_str!("../src/reading.rs")` as READING_SOURCE (exists) and `replay_declaration` (exists, reading.rs:4337). The test itself is added in step 6.

demonstrations.method: Update the briefs.rs tests: `the_reader_brief_names_each_reading_rule_in_one_short_line` (count 6 to 7, `check_speed_timeline` added to its check list, comment updated) keeps the 220-character line cap and the 2400-byte section cap. A new test `the_reader_brief_says_what_a_timeline_assumption_holds` finds the rule line in the rendered reader brief.
demonstrations.observes: The rendered `# Reading rules` section has seven lines. One names `check_speed_timeline`, `Timeline:`, a crates/ path, `stages:`, measured durations and where the delay sits. Each line is at most 220 characters and the section is under 2400 bytes.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the rule line the count is 6 and the named-check loop fails for `check_speed_timeline`.
demonstrations.seam: `reader_brief(&reader_inputs(&reading()))` (briefs.rs:2251; test helper at briefs.rs:4385, both exist). `READING_RULES` is the constant that step 4 changes. No fake is needed.

demonstrations.method: The corpus test from criterion 3 also reads docs/decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md with whitespace collapsed. It asserts that decisions.md holds `## D163`, `check_speed_timeline`, the three alternatives (prompt-only guidance, planner-stage check, reading gate check), the cause wording and the crates/ limit. It asserts that the changelog holds `check_speed_timeline`, 'higher refusal rate is intended', 'expected 5% of newly refused readings' and D163. The decision-log guard confirms the new entry is well formed and appended.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus speed_timeline_refusal_is_declared_intended && cargo test -p athena-cli the_decision_log_is_well_formed_and_only_appended_to
demonstrations.observes: Both pass. The string assertions hold, and `check_log` (decisions.rs:218) finds D163 in order with a Provenance bullet and the pinned prefix unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the D163 entry or the changelog entry the string assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: include_str of `../../../CHANGELOG.md` (the form the existing test uses at refusal_corpus.rs:1141, exists) and `../../../docs/decisions.md` (same relative form). The guard `check_log` exists.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks Athena runs. No existing test is removed or ignored. The only edit to an existing assertion is the rule count 6 to 7 in briefs.rs, forced by the added rule. The full run includes every drain test, each of which passes a request through the fake reader and the real gate in a fixture repo with no crates/ directory. This shows both that an ordinary (non-speed) `ask` still reaches an accepted reading and that the speed request at drain.rs:7008 passes.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0. `a_speed_improving_request_is_read_as_urgent_with_a_reason_and_an_ordinary_one_is_not` (drain.rs:7008) passes because the fake's fixed Timeline passes `check_speed_timeline` and, through the absence phrase, `check_reading_references`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the fake.rs line the drain test fails: the request is refused twice by `check_speed_timeline`. With a bare crates/ path in the fake (no absence phrase), every fixture-based drain test fails in `check_reading_references`.
demonstrations.seam: Whole workspace. `athena_agent::fake::deterministic_turn` (fake.rs:195, exists) is the injected reader in drain.rs:6904 (exists). Step 5 adds the fixed assumption. The fake holds no check logic.
